content:
batteries#1602 by Chad Sharp, which verifies Batteries.BinaryHeap, has been merged. It changes the API: the heap now takes an Ord α instance instead of a lt : α → α → Bool parameter, in line with core's TreeMap and friends.

What changes:

  • BinaryHeap α lt becomes BinaryHeap α with [Ord α], and the operations no longer take lt.
  • Array.heapSort a lt becomes a.heapSort. It still sorts ascending.
  • Batteries.Vector.toBinaryHeap becomes Vector.toBinaryHeap, so v.toBinaryHeap works.

To migrate, turn a custom comparator into an Ord instance, or use Ord.opposite for a min-heap.

In return you get proofs that every operation preserves the heap invariant, plus permutation and sortedness lemmas for heapSort. Compiled heapSort is also about 4x faster on 10^6 Nats.

Mathlib needed no changes. If you depend on BinaryHeap outside Mathlib and hit trouble, please let us know here.
Am I right in saying that the BinaryHeap type is not in and of itself anything but a wrapper?
Wow thanks @cmlsharp! I've been working around the missing API of BinaryHeap in a current project, so this is a very welcome addition :)
